s: A company is building a new data lake on Amazon S3. Data will be processed by AWS Glue jobs and queried with Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift Spectrum. The security team wants a single place to grant database-, table- and column-level permissions to IAM users and roles, and to audit those permissions, instead of maintaining complex S3 bucket policies and IAM policies for every dataset. Which service should the solutions architect use?

w.y: Lake Formation centralizes data lake permissions: it grants database, table and column (and row or cell, through data filters) permissions on the Data Catalog, and integrated services such as Athena, Redshift Spectrum and AWS Glue enforce them. It replaces per-dataset bucket and IAM policies with one permissions model.

o.A: Correct. Central, fine-grained data lake permissions that the analytics services enforce.
o.B: Access points simplify access to shared buckets with per-application policies, but they work at the bucket and prefix level, not on tables or columns.
o.C: IAM Identity Center manages workforce sign-in and permission sets for accounts and applications, not table- and column-level data permissions.
o.D: Macie finds sensitive data; it does not grant or enforce access.
